providers.title: Whitehead for simplicial sets
providers.scope: An n-quasi-isomorphism of simplicial sets induces isomorphisms on homology below n and a surjection in degree n.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Free abelian sheaves, enough points
providers.scope: On a topos with enough points, the free abelian functor carries n-quasi-isomorphisms of simplicial sheaves to n-quasi-isomorphisms.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Free abelian sheaves, homomorphisms
providers.scope: On any topos, the free abelian functor carries n-quasi-isomorphisms of simplicial abelian sheaves to n-quasi-isomorphisms; no hypothesis on points.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Dold-Puppe bound
providers.scope: A functor of degree at most k, extended to complexes through the Dold-Kan correspondence, carries complexes in degrees at most b to normalized complexes in degrees at most kb.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Homotopy invariance
providers.scope: The extension of a non-additive functor to complexes carries homotopic maps to homotopic maps.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Deligne-Lazard theorem
providers.scope: A module over a ring of a topos is flat exactly when it is the local inductive limit of a local system of finite free modules.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The left derived functor
providers.scope: A functor of finite degree has a left derived functor on bounded-above complexes, computed by flat resolutions and compatible with local inductive limits of uniformly bounded complexes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Koszul sequences
providers.scope: For an exact sequence of flat modules, the two Koszul complexes give exact sequences relating symmetric, exterior and divided powers.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The shift formulas
providers.scope: LS^n(E[1]) is (LΛ^n E)[n] and LΛ^n(E[1]) is (LΓ^n E)[n], canonically, for E in the bounded-above derived category; Proposition 3.4 gives the compatibility with products, without sign for the first formula and with the sign (-1)^{mn} for the second.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Décalage is homotopically trivial
providers.scope: Both décalages of a simplicial object, in any category, are homotopy equivalent to the constant object on their augmentation.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The total décalage
providers.scope: The two augmentations of the diagonal of the total décalage are homotopic; Example 1.4 shows that they are not homotopy equivalences in general.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Nerves of internal categories
providers.scope: Nine equivalent conditions characterizing nerves of internal categories in a category with fibre products, including the Segal conditions and cartesian décalage squares; Remark 2.5 shows two weaker conditions that do not suffice.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Groupoids
providers.scope: Seven equivalent conditions for an internal category to be a groupoid, in terms of its nerve and its décalages.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Actions of monoids
providers.scope: Nerves of monoid actions are exactly the simplicial objects over the nerve of the monoid that split as a product with their vertices.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Quillen's comparison
providers.scope: The first and last vertex functors from the category of simplices are weak equivalences, and so is the last-vertex map of a simplicial set; Corollary 3.4: a category and its opposite have the same homotopy type.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Simplices of strict simplicial sets
providers.scope: The nerve of the category of simplices of a strict simplicial set has the homology of its alternating face complex, naturally; Corollary 2.4 computes the truncated categories of injective ordinals.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deligne's theorem
providers.scope: For every p, the inclusion of the ordinals with at least p+2 elements into those with at least p+1 elements, with injective maps, induces a quasi-isomorphism of chains; Corollary 4.3: these categories are weakly contractible.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived colimits
providers.scope: The colimit over a small category has a left derived functor on bounded-above complexes, computed by the simplicial replacement; Corollary 2.4 gives its adjunction with constant diagrams.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Colimits over injective ordinals
providers.scope: Over the category of finite ordinals and injective maps, a complex whose cohomology is eventually locally constant has the cohomology of its value at any stage from which it is locally constant.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The total topos
providers.scope: The total topos of a fibred topos is the category of sheaves on an explicit total site.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The second total topos
providers.scope: For a good fibred topos whose left adjoints preserve fibre products, the second total category is a topos; Proposition 5.1 identifies it, for a diagram in a topos, with the diagrams over it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Direct images
providers.scope: A morphism of fibred topoi induces a morphism of total topoi whose direct image is a limit over comma categories; global sections of the total topos are the limit of the global sections of the levels.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Modules on total topoi
providers.scope: Modules over a ring of a total topos are compatible families of modules; tensor products are computed levelwise, and so are internal Homs from a cartesian module.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Enough levelwise acyclic sheaves
providers.scope: Every abelian sheaf on a total topos is a subsheaf of an injective sheaf whose levels are totally acyclic; for flat transition morphisms, every module is a submodule of an injective module with injective levels.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Standard resolutions
providers.scope: The two standard resolutions of an abelian sheaf on a total topos are exact and become contractible on the levels.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cohomology of total topoi
providers.scope: The derived direct image from a total topos to a topos is computed by the cosimplicial complex of the direct images of the levels, and by the complex of the direct images themselves when the levels are totally acyclic.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived limits
providers.scope: The derived functors of the inverse limit of abelian groups over a small category are the cohomology of its cosimplicial complex; Corollary 3.7 gives the spectral sequence from derived limits of the cohomology of the levels.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Final objects
providers.scope: Over an index category with a final object, the derived direct image of a total topos is that of the final level.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Levelwise direct images
providers.scope: Derived direct images under a morphism of fibred topoi over a fixed index category commute with restriction to the levels.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Simplicial topoi
providers.scope: The derived direct image from a simplicial topos to a topos is computed by the cosimplicial object of the direct images of the levels; Corollary 2.2 gives the spectral sequence from the higher direct images of the levels, and Theorem 2.3 the multisimplicial case.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The associated simplicial topos
providers.scope: The cohomology of the total topos of any fibred topos is that of an associated simplicial topos.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Décalage of a simplicial topos
providers.scope: The décalage of a simplicial topos has the cohomology of the level onto which it is augmented.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Free abelian sheaves and descent
providers.scope: For a simplicial object X of a topos, Rp_*p^*E is RHom(Z(X), E); Corollary 5.3 gives cohomological descent for hypercoverings in every topos, and Corollary 5.4 the invariance under morphisms inducing quasi-isomorphisms of free abelian sheaves.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The second total topos
providers.scope: For a complex whose levels stay totally acyclic under all inverse images, the derived direct image from the second total topos is that of the associated simplicial object.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Local systems
providers.scope: Cartesian objects of the two total topoi correspond, and their cohomologies agree; Corollary 3.5 computes the cohomology of simplicial sheaves over a simplicial object.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Base change
providers.scope: A criterion for derived direct images on the second total topoi to commute with restriction to the levels.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Left derived functors of u_!
providers.scope: Under an exactness condition on flat modules, the left adjoint of the inverse image of modules on total topoi has a left derived functor on bounded above complexes, computed by standard resolutions of flat complexes, with RHom(Lu_!E, F) = RHom(E, u^*F).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived colimits and constant diagrams
providers.scope: For diagrams of modules over a ring of a topos, the derived colimit and the constant diagram functor satisfy RHom(L colim E, F) = RHom(E, cF).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Local inductive limits
providers.scope: For a locally filtering diagram in a topos, the left adjoint of the inverse image of modules is the local inductive limit, which is exact.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived left adjoints on the second total topos
providers.scope: Under exactness conditions on flat modules, the left adjoint of the inverse image on the second total topos has a left derived functor, adjoint to the inverse image on RHom complexes and computed levelwise for morphisms over a fixed index category.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Décalage for left adjoints
providers.scope: The derived colimit of a simplicial module is its chain complex (Lemma 4.1), and the décalage of a simplicial topos is trivial for the derived left adjoint of its augmentation.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The internal mixed Hom
providers.scope: For a diagram in a topos, the internal Hom from modules of the first total topos to modules of the second, with values in the second total topos.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The duality formula
providers.scope: RHom on the first total topos into a module pulled back from the topos is RGamma of the second total topos of the derived internal mixed Hom.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The relative duality formula
providers.scope: For a morphism of diagrams u, the canonical map from the internal mixed Hom of Lu_!E to Ru_* of the internal mixed Hom of E is an isomorphism for coefficients pulled back from the topos.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Equivariant sheaves and their nerves
providers.scope: The category BX of equivariant sheaves on a simplicial topos has colimits and finite limits computed on X_0, and its two nerves into the total topoi are fully faithful.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Images of the nerves
providers.scope: An object of the first (second) total topos is isomorphic to a nerve exactly when its maps along simplicial maps fixing the last (first) vertex are isomorphisms.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Nerves of internal categories
providers.scope: The simplicial topos of the nerve of an internal category of a topos is a good two-sided pseudo-category.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Coinduction
providers.scope: On a pseudo-category, the coinduced sheaf s_*t^*L carries a canonical equivariant structure, and coinduction is right adjoint to the forgetful functor.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Induction
providers.scope: On a good pseudo-category, the induced sheaf t_!s^*L carries a canonical equivariant structure, and induction is left adjoint to the forgetful functor.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Equivariant modules
providers.scope: Equivariant modules form an abelian category with enough injectives, the direct summands of coinduced injectives; on a good pseudo-category every module is a quotient of an induced free module.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Homotopies of Roos complexes
providers.scope: A natural transformation between two functors gives an explicit homotopy between the maps they induce on Roos complexes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Nerves of coinduced modules
providers.scope: The nerves of a coinduced module are the direct images along the décalage of its pullback by the last vertex, and the derived direct images when the module is injective and the inverse images along last vertices preserve injectives.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Nerves of induced modules
providers.scope: On a good two-sided pseudo-category, under an exactness condition on flat modules, the nerve of an induced flat module is the derived left adjoint along the décalage of its pullback by the first vertex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cohomology of BX
providers.scope: If the inverse images along the last vertices preserve injective modules, the nerves compute RHom out of complexes with invertible structure; Corollary 4.2 gives the cohomology of BX and its spectral sequence from the levels.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived Hom of equivariant modules
providers.scope: Under an exactness condition on left adjoints as well, the second nerve, and the first for two-sided pseudo-categories, computes all RHom complexes and is fully faithful on bounded derived categories.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Group cohomology
providers.scope: For a group acting on a point, the complex of the levels is the inhomogeneous cochain complex of group cohomology.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Direct images to a base
providers.scope: For a pseudo-category over a topos, the derived direct image of an equivariant module to the topos is computed on either total topos.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The mixed Hom functor
providers.scope: For a good fibred topos with a cartesian ring, the derived mixed Hom from modules on the second total topos to modules on the first, with values in functors on the index category, computed by complexes with injective levels.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Mixed Hom and inverse images
providers.scope: For a morphism over the index category, RHom^!(L, Rf_*M) and RHom^!(Lf^*L, M) are canonically isomorphic for L bounded above.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Mixed Hom and derived left adjoints
providers.scope: Under exactness conditions on flat modules, RHom^!(Lf_!E, F) and RHom^!(E, f^*F) are canonically isomorphic for E bounded above.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Ext groups of equivariant modules
providers.scope: Under the injectivity and exactness conditions, RHom_BX(E, F) is the derived limit over the simplex category of the mixed Hom from the second nerve of E to the nerve of F; Corollary 3.4 gives a spectral sequence from the Ext groups on the levels.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Ext over a group ring
providers.scope: For a group acting on a point, Ext over the group ring into a module injective over the coefficients is computed by cochains of the group with values in Hom groups.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Reduced spectral diagrams
providers.scope: Translating down by one in every coordinate is an equivalence from reduced spectral diagrams to large simplicial diagrams; reduction is its left adjoint on all spectral diagrams.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Spectra of commutative group objects
providers.scope: The spectrum of iterated nerves is fully faithful on commutative group objects, with image the spectral diagrams of iterated nerves whose structure maps are isomorphisms.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived categories of spectral diagrams
providers.scope: The bounded above derived category embeds fully faithfully in that of spectral diagrams, with image the objects whose cohomology consists of spectra of objects.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The suspension theorem
providers.scope: For a reduced functor and an n-reduced simplicial object, the suspension is an isomorphism in degrees below 2n and onto in degree 2n.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The stabilization
providers.scope: The homology of the stabilization of F at X in degree i is the homology of F of the n-th suspension of X in degree i+n, for every n > i.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Stabilization and triangles
providers.scope: The stabilization is additive and carries degreewise split exact sequences to distinguished triangles, through its shift isomorphism.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Exactness of stable derived functors
providers.scope: The stable derived functor, extended to bounded above complexes with its shift isomorphism, is an exact functor of triangulated categories.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Symmetric, exterior and divided powers
providers.scope: The stable derived functor of the n-th symmetric power is that of the exterior power shifted by n-1, which is that of the divided power shifted by n-1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Lifting against fibrant quasi-isomorphisms
providers.scope: A fibrant quasi-isomorphism of simplicial modules in a topos has local lifts against finite monomorphisms of simplicial sets.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Fractions for simplicial modules and algebras
providers.scope: Over a simplicial ring of a topos, quasi-isomorphisms of modules up to homotopy admit left and right fractions, and quasi-isomorphisms of algebras admit right fractions.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Suspension and loops
providers.scope: On the derived category of a simplicial ring, the suspension is left adjoint to the loop functor and fully faithful, with image the modules whose homotopy vanishes in degree 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Long exact Ext sequences
providers.scope: Distinguished triangles of simplicial modules give long exact sequences of Ext groups in both variables.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Constant rings
providers.scope: For a ring placed in every degree, normalization carries the distinguished triangles of simplicial modules to those of the derived category, and the extension class to the connecting morphism.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The first Ext group by extensions
providers.scope: Every class in the first Ext group is the class of an extension of simplicial modules after a quasi-isomorphism, with a criterion for two extensions to give the same class.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Flat modules and quasi-isomorphisms
providers.scope: Tensoring with a degreewise flat simplicial module preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and so does tensoring a quasi-isomorphism of flat modules with any module.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The derived tensor product
providers.scope: The tensor product of simplicial modules over a simplicial ring has a left derived functor, computed by a flat replacement of either factor.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Quasi-isomorphic simplicial rings
providers.scope: A quasi-isomorphism of simplicial rings induces an equivalence of derived categories, through derived extension and restriction of scalars.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Tor spectral sequence
providers.scope: The homology of a derived tensor product of simplicial modules is the abutment of a spectral sequence starting from the homology of the degreewise Tor modules.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Künneth spectral sequence
providers.scope: A spectral sequence from Tor over the homology ring of the simplicial ring, of the homology modules of the factors, converges to the homology of their derived tensor product.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Bounded derived categories of differential graded modules
providers.scope: Over a differential graded ring in nonpositive degrees, the localizations of the categories of bounded modules are full subcategories of the derived category, cut out by bounds on cohomology.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Truncated differential graded rings
providers.scope: Modules with cohomology in an interval of length at most n over a ring in nonpositive degrees are the same as modules over its truncated ring t_n.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Bounded resolutions of differential graded modules
providers.scope: Bounded above modules have functorial good resolutions with the same bound, and bounded below modules have K-injective resolutions with the same bound.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived Hom of differential graded modules
providers.scope: Derived Hom and derived internal Hom are defined on all modules, compute morphisms in the derived category, and respect bounds for rings in nonpositive degrees.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Extension of scalars for differential graded rings
providers.scope: Derived extension of scalars is left adjoint to restriction, also on derived Hom, and a quasi-isomorphism of rings gives an equivalence of derived categories.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Normalization and derived tensor products
providers.scope: Normalization carries the derived tensor products and extensions of scalars of simplicial modules over a simplicial ring to those of differential graded modules over its normalized complex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Graded objects as equivariant sheaves
providers.scope: Graded objects of a topos are the equivariant sheaves on the simplicial topos of the categories C_•(J), and C_• is their second nerve, fully faithful with an explicit image.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Nerves of graded actions
providers.scope: For a graded monoid G, the bisimplicial nerve Ner(C_•(G), C_•(X)) is a fully faithful functor of the graded G-object X, with essential image given by two isomorphism conditions.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Base change along discrete opfibrations
providers.scope: A cartesian square of diagrams in a topos with one side a discrete opfibration induces a square of topoi with invertible base change map.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The pseudo-category of a graded action
providers.scope: When the products of the grading are isomorphisms, the simplicial topos of the nerve of a graded action is a good two-sided pseudo-category whose levels are localizations of one topos.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: External tensor products of multisimplicial objects
providers.scope: Normalization, reduction and translation commute with external tensor products of multisimplicial objects.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Induced modules over rings of type C_•(J)
providers.scope: Modules over a ring of type C_•(J) form a Grothendieck abelian category; induced modules are left adjoint to the forgetful functor and exact when the ring is flat.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Large simplicial rings and spectral rings
providers.scope: Translation by one is an equivalence between large simplicial rings and reduced spectral rings, and reduction is left adjoint to the inclusion of reduced spectral rings.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Bilinear maps as maps of spectra
providers.scope: Bilinear maps of abelian sheaves are the maps between their spectra of the type given by concatenation of coordinates.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Spectra of modules
providers.scope: A module over a ring is determined by its spectrum, a graded object with an action of the spectrum of the ring, with an explicit essential image.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Modules as bisimplicial diagrams
providers.scope: Modules over a ring are the bisimplicial diagrams built from products of copies of the ring and the module that satisfy four isomorphism conditions.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Reduction and translation in derived categories
providers.scope: Translation by one is fully faithful from the derived category of modules over a ring of type C_•(S_0) to that over the corresponding reduced ring of type C_•(S_1), with reduction as left adjoint.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The diagonal comparison functor
providers.scope: The normalized double diagonal is an exact functor from modules over a ring of type C_•(S_0) to differential graded modules over its diagonal ring, and it respects upper bounds.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived colimits over the nerve of the injective ordinals
providers.scope: The derived colimit of a coefficient system on the simplices of the nerve is the total complex of the sum of its values over the simplices of each dimension.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The constant functor and its left adjoint
providers.scope: The constant functor into objects of type C_•(S_0) is fully faithful on bounded above derived categories, with the normalized double diagonal as left adjoint.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Objects with constant cohomology
providers.scope: A bounded above object of type C_•(S_0) comes from a complex of abelian sheaves exactly when its cohomology objects are constant, and similarly for reduced spectral objects.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The comparison theorem for diagonal rings
providers.scope: For a ring of type C_•(S_0) with flat components, derived Hom into a module with constant underlying object is computed over the normalized double diagonal ring.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Comparison for reduced spectral rings
providers.scope: The comparison theorem transferred to rings of type C_•(S_1) through reduction and translation.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived tensor products of rings
providers.scope: The derived tensor product of two rings is a differential graded ring in degrees -1 and 0, computed from any flat presentation of one factor.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The stable ring of a ring
providers.scope: The stabilization of the free abelian group functor at a ring is a simplicial ring with flat terms, augmented to the ring by a ring homomorphism.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived tensor products through the stable ring
providers.scope: The truncated normalized stable ring is a flat presentation of the ring, so the derived tensor product of two rings is a truncation of a normalized simplicial ring.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Mac Lane's theorem
providers.scope: The derived tensor product of the ring with the stable module of a module, over the normalized stable ring, is the module.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Bar resolutions
providers.scope: The bar construction of a module over a ring homomorphism is contractible over the smaller ring, and a flat resolution when the ring and the module are flat over it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Mac Lane resolution
providers.scope: A module has a functorial resolution by sums of direct summands of the free modules on the products of copies of the ring and the module.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Base change of the comparison theorem
providers.scope: The comparison theorem for diagonal rings holds for a ring with flat components tensored with any commutative ring.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Ext groups through spectra
providers.scope: Derived Hom from the free module on the spectrum of a module into the spectrum of a complex of modules is the derived Hom of modules.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Spectra over a derived tensor product
providers.scope: Bounded complexes over the derived tensor product of a ring with a commutative ring have spectra, extending those of complexes of modules and compatible with derived Hom.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Two consecutive degrees
providers.scope: The spectrum over a derived tensor product is fully faithful on complexes with cohomology in two consecutive degrees, with an explicit essential image.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Spectra and tensor products
providers.scope: The spectrum over a derived tensor product commutes with derived tensor products over the coefficient ring when the result is bounded.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Ext groups as cohomology of spectral nerves
providers.scope: The Ext groups of modules are the cohomology of the total topos of the nerve of the action of the spectrum of the ring on the spectrum of the first module.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Relative cohomology and cones
providers.scope: Relative cohomology along a homomorphism of modules computes derived Hom out of its cone.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Quasi-coherent modules on the big fppf site
providers.scope: Quasi-coherent sheaves of a scheme and quasi-coherent modules on its big fppf site correspond, with the same cohomology.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Adequate modules
providers.scope: Adequate modules on the big site have quasi-coherent direct images on the Zariski site, no higher direct images, and direct images compatible with flat base change.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Truncated pullbacks to the big site
providers.scope: A bounded complex with quasi-coherent cohomology is recovered from the truncation of its pullback to the big fppf site.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived Hom on the big site
providers.scope: Derived Hom into a bounded complex with quasi-coherent cohomology is the same on the Zariski site and, after truncation, on the big fppf site.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Flat base change for adequate complexes
providers.scope: Direct images to the Zariski site of complexes with adequate cohomology commute with flat base change.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Perfect complexes on the big site
providers.scope: Complexes of perfect amplitude in [a, b] on the Zariski site and on the big fppf site of a scheme are equivalent.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Diagrams of schemes
providers.scope: The comparison holds for diagrams of schemes, and quasi-cartesian objects on the big site are those with cartesian cohomology.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cotangent complex of a morphism of diagrams
providers.scope: The cotangent complex of a morphism of diagrams of schemes is, at every level, the cotangent complex of the level, with the functoriality maps as structure maps.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Transitivity triangle for diagrams
providers.scope: Morphisms of diagrams X to Y to Z give a natural transitivity triangle, whose connecting map is the Kodaira-Spencer class.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Tor-independent base change for schemes
providers.scope: The cotangent complex of a morphism of schemes commutes with Tor-independent base change, so cartesian Tor-independent diagrams have quasi-cartesian cotangent complexes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Extensions of diagrams as ringed-topos extensions
providers.scope: Square-zero extensions of a diagram of schemes by a termwise quasi-coherent ideal are the algebra extensions on its Zariski topos.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Classification of extensions of diagrams
providers.scope: Extensions of a diagram of schemes are classified by Ext^1 of its cotangent complex, with automorphisms Ext^0, also computable on the big fppf site.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deformations of a morphism of schemes
providers.scope: A thickening of a morphism of schemes has an isomorphism on ideals exactly when its square is cartesian and a Tor_1 group vanishes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deformations of squares
providers.scope: Deformations of commutative squares of schemes carry cartesian squares to cartesian squares.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deformations of a morphism over a thickened target
providers.scope: Lifting a morphism of diagrams over a square-zero thickening of its target is obstructed in Ext^2 by the product of the Kodaira-Spencer class and the class of the thickening; lifts form an Ext^1-torsor.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deformed diagrams of morphisms
providers.scope: A deformation of a morphism over a deformation of its target deforms the diagram the morphism defines and keeps its cartesian squares cartesian.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Nerves of action categories
providers.scope: The nerve of the action category of a category scheme acting on a sheaf is the pullback of the nerve of the category scheme along its first vertex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Equivariant sheaves over an equivariant sheaf
providers.scope: Sheaves equivariant for the action category of a G-sheaf L are the G-sheaves over L.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The opposite action category
providers.scope: The nerve functor from the bounded derived category of the opposite action category to the fppf total topos of the nerve is fully faithful, with an explicit essential image.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Action groupoids
providers.scope: For a groupoid scheme, inversion identifies the action category with its opposite.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Tor independence and base change
providers.scope: When P and R are Tor independent over Q, Tor independence of P and R' over Q is Tor independence of P x_Q R and R' over R.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The equivariant cotangent complex
providers.scope: For a morphism of G-schemes Tor independent of G, the truncated pullbacks of the cotangent complex of the nerves descend uniquely to the derived category of the opposite action category.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Properties of the equivariant cotangent complex
providers.scope: The equivariant cotangent complex has the expected underlying complex, is bounded for local complete intersections, and is the trivial pullback for trivial actions.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Ext groups of the equivariant cotangent complex
providers.scope: Ext groups of the equivariant cotangent complex into quasi-coherent equivariant modules are Ext groups of the cotangent complex of the nerves on the Zariski total topos.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Equivariant Kodaira-Spencer class
providers.scope: Morphisms X to Y to Z of G-schemes give equivariant transitivity maps, the equivariant Kodaira-Spencer class and long exact sequences of Ext groups.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Change of the category scheme
providers.scope: Restriction along an internal functor G' to G gives a base change map of equivariant cotangent complexes, an isomorphism under Tor independence.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Closed immersions into smooth schemes
providers.scope: For a closed immersion into a smooth scheme, the first truncation of the cotangent complex is isomorphic to the conormal complex, and the Kodaira-Spencer class is a universal sign times the differential on H^-1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Equivariant conormal complexes
providers.scope: For an equivariant closed immersion into a smooth G-scheme, the truncated equivariant cotangent complex is isomorphic to the equivariant conormal complex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Recognizing nerves of action categories
providers.scope: Simplicial objects over N(G) whose levels are the pullbacks of level 0 along the first vertex are nerves of action categories.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Equivariant extensions and extensions of nerves
providers.scope: Equivariant extensions are the extensions of the nerves whose ideal is cartesian along the faces fixing the first vertex; Tor independence makes the condition automatic.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Classification of equivariant extensions
providers.scope: Equivariant extensions of a G-scheme are classified by Ext^1 of the equivariant cotangent complex, with automorphisms Ext^0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Equivariant deformations and nerves
providers.scope: Equivariant deformations of a morphism are the deformations of its nerve over the nerve of the thickened target.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Equivariant deformations of a morphism
providers.scope: Equivariant deformations over an equivariant extension are obstructed in Ext^2 of the equivariant cotangent complex by the product of the equivariant Kodaira-Spencer class and the class of the extension; they form an Ext^1-torsor.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Spectral sequence of the obstruction
providers.scope: A spectral sequence over the nerve computes the equivariant Ext groups, and its edge map carries the equivariant obstruction to the obstruction for the underlying morphism of schemes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Lifting maps to square-zero extensions
providers.scope: A ring map lifts to given square-zero extensions exactly when two classes in Ext^1 of the cotangent complex agree; the lifts form a torsor under derivations.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Morphisms between equivariant extensions
providers.scope: An equivariant morphism lifts to given equivariant extensions exactly when a class in Ext^1 vanishes; the lifts form an Ext^0-torsor.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Frobenius kernels
providers.scope: The n-fold relative Frobenius of a group scheme over a field is a homomorphism and a universal homeomorphism; its kernel is a finite connected normal subgroup scheme, compatible with closed subgroups.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The first Frobenius kernel
providers.scope: The first Frobenius kernel of a group scheme locally of finite type over a field is a truncated polynomial algebra, hence a local complete intersection.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Quotients by Frobenius kernels
providers.scope: Over a perfect field, the quotient of a group scheme of finite type by a large enough Frobenius kernel is the reduced subgroup of a Frobenius twist, hence smooth.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Group schemes over a field are local complete intersections
providers.scope: Every group scheme locally of finite type over a field is a local complete intersection over the field.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Flat group schemes are syntomic
providers.scope: A group scheme flat and locally of finite presentation over a scheme is syntomic, and its cotangent complex is locally a two-term complex of finite free modules in degrees -1 and 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The cotangent complex at the unit
providers.scope: For a group scheme over a field, the derived pullback of the cotangent complex to the unit has H^0 dual to the Lie algebra and H^-1 of dimension dim Lie - dim G; it vanishes exactly for smooth groups.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Trivial torsors
providers.scope: A torsor with a section is isomorphic to the trivial torsor through the section.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Torsors and Cech nerves
providers.scope: A torsor under a flat group scheme locally of finite presentation is syntomic and surjective, and the nerve of the action is the Cech nerve of the torsor.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Descent along a torsor
providers.scope: Pullback is an equivalence from modules on the big fppf site of the base onto equivariant modules on the torsor, with quasi-inverse the invariant sections.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Descent on big sites
providers.scope: Pullback to the nerve of a torsor is fully faithful on bounded derived categories of the big fppf sites, with essential image the quasi-cartesian objects.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Descent on Zariski sites
providers.scope: Pullback to the nerve of a torsor is fully faithful on bounded complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology on the Zariski sites, with essential image the quasi-cartesian objects with termwise quasi-coherent cohomology.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Direct images, sections and equivariant complexes
providers.scope: A descended complex is the derived direct image of its pullback to the nerve, its pullback along a section, and the invariant direct image of its equivariant form.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Truncating a distinguished triangle
providers.scope: Truncating the first two vertices of a distinguished triangle whose third vertex lies in degrees at least n gives a distinguished triangle.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The co-Lie complex and the Atiyah triangle
providers.scope: The cotangent complex of the nerves of a torsor descends to a perfect complex of tor amplitude [-1,0] on the base, and the transitivity triangle descends to the Atiyah triangle, whose third map is the Atiyah class.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Base change of the co-Lie complex
providers.scope: The co-Lie complex of a torsor commutes with arbitrary base change of the base.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Equivariant complexes of a torsor
providers.scope: The equivariant cotangent complexes of a torsor are the pullbacks of its co-Lie complexes, and the equivariant Kodaira-Spencer class is the pullback of the Atiyah class.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The co-Lie complex of a smooth group
providers.scope: For a smooth group scheme the co-Lie complex of a torsor is the co-Lie module twisted by the torsor through the coadjoint action.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Atiyah sequence
providers.scope: For a smooth group scheme the Atiyah triangle gives an exact sequence of invariant differential forms, whose class is the Atiyah class when the base is smooth.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deformations of a torsor are torsors
providers.scope: Equivariant deformations of a torsor over a first-order thickening of the base are torsors, and conversely.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The class of the thickened nerve
providers.scope: The class of the thickening of the nerve of the base is the pullback of the class of the thickening.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deformations of torsors
providers.scope: Deformations of a torsor over a first-order thickening are obstructed in Ext^2 of the co-Lie complex by the product of the class of the thickening and the Atiyah class; they form an Ext^1-torsor with automorphism groups Ext^0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Duality and smooth groups
providers.scope: The groups classifying deformations of a torsor are cohomology groups of the dual of the co-Lie complex; torsors over affine bases always deform, and for smooth groups the coefficients are the adjoint bundle.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The co-Lie complex of a group scheme
providers.scope: The co-Lie complex of a flat group scheme locally of finite presentation is perfect of tor amplitude [-1,0], has the invariant differentials as H^0, and is the co-Lie complex of the group as a torsor.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Base change of the co-Lie complex of a group
providers.scope: The co-Lie complex of a flat group scheme commutes with arbitrary base change.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Smoothness and the co-Lie complex
providers.scope: A flat group scheme locally of finite presentation is smooth exactly when its co-Lie complex has tor amplitude [0,0].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Exact sequences and torsors
providers.scope: In an exact sequence of flat group schemes the quotient map is a torsor under the kernel.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The triangle of an exact sequence
providers.scope: An exact sequence of flat group schemes gives a distinguished triangle of co-Lie complexes, with the functoriality maps in degree 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The long exact sequence of co-Lie complexes
providers.scope: An exact sequence of flat group schemes gives a six-term exact sequence of the cohomology of co-Lie complexes; the map from the quotient is an isomorphism exactly when the kernel is etale.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Descent along a torsor over a diagram
providers.scope: For a torsor under a flat group scheme over a diagram of schemes, pullback to the nerve of the action is fully faithful on bounded complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology, with an explicit essential image.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The co-Lie complex of a torsor over a diagram
providers.scope: A torsor over a diagram of schemes has a quasi-cartesian co-Lie complex with perfect levels and an Atiyah triangle, restricting levelwise to those of the torsors over the schemes of the diagram.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The adjoint co-Lie complex
providers.scope: The co-Lie complex of a flat group scheme carries an action of the group, obtained by descent along the universal torsor over the nerve, as an object of the derived category of the classifying topos.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The coadjoint action on invariant forms
providers.scope: On invariant differential forms the action is the coadjoint action, and for a smooth group the adjoint co-Lie complex is this module in degree 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The cotangent complex of the nerve of a group scheme
providers.scope: The cotangent complex of the nerve of a flat group scheme sits in a distinguished triangle between a copy of the co-Lie complex at each vertex and the adjoint co-Lie complex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Relative Ext groups of the adjoint co-Lie complex
providers.scope: The Ext groups of the cotangent complex of the nerve are relative Ext groups of the adjoint co-Lie complex on the classifying topos, computed by a spectral sequence from Ext groups on the powers of the group.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deformations of group schemes and of their nerves
providers.scope: Deformations of a flat group scheme over a first-order thickening are the same as deformations of the morphism from its nerve to the base.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deformations of flat group schemes
providers.scope: A flat group scheme deforms over a first-order thickening exactly when an obstruction in Ext^2 of the cotangent complex of its nerve vanishes; deformations then form a torsor under Ext^1, with automorphisms Ext^0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Smooth affine groups and Hochschild cochains
providers.scope: For a smooth affine group over an affine base, the deformation groups are the cohomology of cochains of the group with values in its Lie algebra tensored with the ideal.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Extending homomorphisms to deformations
providers.scope: A homomorphism of flat group schemes extends to given deformations exactly when a class in Ext^1 vanishes; the extensions then form a torsor under Ext^0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deforming a homomorphism with a given target
providers.scope: Deformations of a flat group scheme together with an extension of a homomorphism to a given deformation of the target are classified by Ext groups of the relative cotangent complex of the nerves.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The shear isomorphism
providers.scope: For a group scheme H over a diagram Y, the cotangent complex of H over Y is the pullback of the co-Lie complex of H.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Additivity of the co-Lie complex
providers.scope: The co-Lie complex of a product is the sum, and for commutative group schemes a sum of homomorphisms induces the sum of the maps of co-Lie complexes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The tensor formula for Lie complexes
providers.scope: For a group scheme over a diagram, the internal mixed Hom from its co-Lie complex into a bounded complex is the derived tensor product with its Lie complex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Torsors under a commutative group
providers.scope: The co-Lie complex of a torsor under a commutative group scheme G, over a scheme or a diagram of schemes, is the pullback of the co-Lie complex of G.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The adjoint co-Lie complex of a commutative group
providers.scope: For a commutative group scheme the adjoint co-Lie complex is the co-Lie complex with the trivial action.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Lie complex of the nerve
providers.scope: The Lie complex of the nerve of a commutative group scheme is the nerve of its Lie complex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Lie complex of the spectrum
providers.scope: The Lie complex of the spectrum of a commutative group scheme is the spectrum of its Lie complex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Second nerves on spectral pseudo-categories
providers.scope: On the pseudo-category of a graded action, the second nerve is fully faithful on bounded derived categories, with image the objects whose cohomology is cartesian along the maps fixing the first vertex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Lie complex of a module scheme
providers.scope: The Lie complex of a module scheme over a ring scheme A has a canonical structure of a complex over the derived tensor product of A and the structure ring, determined by the spectral nerve.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Exact sequences of module schemes
providers.scope: An exact sequence of module schemes gives a distinguished triangle of their Lie complexes over the stable ring with coefficients.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Ext formula
providers.scope: The Ext groups of the cotangent complex of the spectral nerve of a module scheme are Ext groups of modules into its Lie complex with coefficients.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Relative Ext groups of the spectral nerve
providers.scope: Relative Ext groups of the cotangent complex for a homomorphism of module schemes are Ext groups of modules out of its cone.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deformations of module schemes and of their spectral nerves
providers.scope: Deformations of a module scheme over a first-order thickening are the same as deformations of the morphism from its spectral nerve to that of the base.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deformations of module schemes
providers.scope: A module scheme deforms exactly when an obstruction in Ext^2 of modules into its Lie complex tensored with the ideal vanishes; deformations then form a torsor under Ext^1, with automorphisms Ext^0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Extending homomorphisms of module schemes
providers.scope: A homomorphism of module schemes extends to given deformations exactly when a class in Ext^1 vanishes; the extensions then form a torsor under Ext^0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deforming a homomorphism of module schemes with a given target
providers.scope: Deformations of a module scheme together with an extension of a homomorphism to a given deformation of the target are classified by Ext groups of modules into the fibre of the map of Lie complexes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Adjoints of the degree functors on graded modules
providers.scope: The degree-n component functor on graded modules has graded coinduction as right adjoint; placing a module in degree n is right adjoint to the degree-n component after reduction modulo the positive part.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The graded cotangent complex
providers.scope: The graded cotangent complex forgets to the cotangent complex; its degree-zero part is the cotangent complex of the degree-zero rings, and for B^0 = A its degree-one part is B^1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The graded transitivity triangle
providers.scope: Maps of graded rings A -> B -> C give a distinguished triangle of graded cotangent complexes, compatible with forgetting the grading and with degree zero.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Graded square-zero extensions
providers.scope: Graded square-zero extensions are classified by Ext^1 of the graded cotangent complex in the derived category of graded modules, with automorphisms the graded derivations.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Naturality of the Atiyah class of a module
providers.scope: The Atiyah class of a module is natural in the module and in the ring map, and vanishes for modules extended from the base by a flat module.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Atiyah class through the graded cotangent complex
providers.scope: The Atiyah class of a module M is the connecting map of the degree-one part of the graded transitivity triangle of the dual numbers B + M.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Principal parts and connections
providers.scope: Connections on a module correspond to splittings of its principal parts extension, whose class is the image of the Atiyah class.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deformations of modules over a square-zero thickening
providers.scope: An extension of modules with prescribed action of the ideal exists exactly when an obstruction in Ext^2 vanishes; the extensions then form a torsor under Ext^1, with automorphisms Hom.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The obstruction as the product of the Atiyah class and the class of the thickening
providers.scope: The canonical obstruction class of a module over a square-zero thickening is the composite of its Atiyah class and the class of the thickening.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The universal first-order thickening
providers.scope: For the thickening A/K^2 of A/K the canonical class of a module is the class of the two-term truncation of its derived tensor product with A/K over A.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deforming a morphism of modules with given source
providers.scope: Deforming the target of a morphism of modules together with the morphism is governed by the obstruction of the target and a class in a cokernel of Ext^1 groups.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The filtered derived category
providers.scope: Complexes with finite filtrations up to filtered homotopy, localized at the maps that are quasi-isomorphisms on all graded pieces, form a triangulated category; a morphism is an isomorphism when its graded pieces are.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Filtered objects and their Yoneda extensions
providers.scope: Filtered objects form the full subcategory of objects whose graded pieces have cohomology in degree 0, and their filtered Ext groups are the Yoneda extensions with exact graded pieces.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The filtered derived Hom
providers.scope: With enough injectives, the filtered Hom complex into a bounded below complex of injective type computes the filtered derived Hom, and its H^n F^0 is the filtered Ext group.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The spectral sequence of a filtered derived Hom
providers.scope: The filtration of the derived Hom gives a convergent spectral sequence from the Ext groups of the graded pieces, whose first differential is composition with the extension classes, with explicit signs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Graded pieces of a tensor product
providers.scope: If one filtered complex has flat graded pieces, the graded pieces of the tensor product are the tensor products of the graded pieces.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The filtered derived category is symmetric monoidal
providers.scope: The derived tensor product makes the filtered derived category of a ringed topos a symmetric monoidal category, and the underlying complex and the associated graded are symmetric monoidal functors.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cartan's isomorphism for filtered complexes
providers.scope: RHom(L (x) M, N) = RHom(L, RHom(M, N)) on the filtered derived category, compatibly with the associated graded; the filtered derived category is closed symmetric monoidal.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived pullback and pushforward of filtered complexes
providers.scope: Derived pullback is left adjoint to derived pushforward on filtered derived categories, with the internal form RHom(L, Rf_*M) = Rf_* RHom(Lf^*L, M), compatibly with the associated graded.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Duality for perfect filtered complexes
providers.scope: For filtered perfect L, the biduality morphism, the morphism from the dual tensor M to RHom(L, M) and the product of internal Homs are isomorphisms, with no boundedness condition.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Dualizable objects of the filtered derived category
providers.scope: An object of the filtered derived category has a dual exactly when its graded pieces are perfect; the dual is RHom(L, A) with evaluation and an explicit coevaluation.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Additivity of traces
providers.scope: For a filtered perfect complex E and a filtered morphism E (x) K -> E (x) L with K, L unfiltered, the trace on E is the sum of the traces on the graded pieces.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Multiplicativity of traces
providers.scope: The trace of the tensor product of two morphisms of perfect filtered complexes is the tensor product of their traces, on morphisms and internally.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cup products and traces
providers.scope: The cup product of u: E (x) K1 -> F (x) L1 and v: F (x) K2 -> E (x) L2 is additive on graded pieces and multiplicative, and Tr(uv) = Tr(vu) = <u, v> for endomorphism-type pairs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Graded pieces of powers of a filtered module
providers.scope: If the graded pieces of a filtered module are flat, the graded pieces of its symmetric, exterior and divided powers are the corresponding powers of its graded module.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived powers of filtered and graded complexes
providers.scope: Symmetric, exterior and divided powers derive to the bounded above filtered and graded derived categories; the graded pieces of LT^n(L) are sums of derived tensor products of the LT^m(gr^i L).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Amplitude of derived powers
providers.scope: If L has tor or perfect amplitude in an interval [a,b] containing 0, then LT^n(L) has tor or perfect amplitude in [na,nb].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Filtered Koszul sequences
providers.scope: For a sequence of filtered modules with exact flat graded pieces, the Koszul sequences are exact on every filtration step, with graded pieces the Koszul sequences of the graded pieces.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Shift isomorphisms on filtered derived categories
providers.scope: LS^n(M[1]) = LΛ^n(M)[n] and LΛ^n(M[1]) = LΓ^n(M)[n] on the bounded above filtered and graded derived categories, with the shift formulas of complexes as underlying isomorphisms.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Graded pieces of the shift isomorphisms
providers.scope: On graded pieces the shift isomorphisms are sums of tensor products of the shift isomorphisms of the graded pieces, composed with the isomorphisms of shifted tensor products, with the sign (-1)^(sum over i<j of n_i n_j) for the second one.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Diagonal maps and Koszul sequences
providers.scope: The diagonal maps carry the Koszul sequence of an exact sequence tensored with M to the Koszul sequence tensored with S^n M.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived diagonal maps
providers.scope: For filtered complexes concentrated in degrees at most 0: LS^n(L (x) M) -> LS^n L (x) LS^n M and LΛ^n(L (x) M) -> LΛ^n L (x) LS^n M, natural and compatible with graded pieces.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Diagonal maps and shift isomorphisms
providers.scope: The diagonal maps commute with the shift isomorphisms of L (x) M and of L, for L and M concentrated in degrees at most 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
